newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Frankfurt, Milan stocks hit peaks, London dull.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Frankfurt, Milan stocks hit peaks, London dull.

text.p: Stocks in Frankfurt, Milan and Paris climbed strongly on Wednesday, with the German bourse reaching its seventh consecutive record close, but London made only modest gains, dogged by worries over higher interest rates.

On currency markets, the dollar edged up to fresh 41-month peaks against the mark on a subdued economic outlook for Germany, while sterling eased after leaping to a six-year high against the mark on expectations of higher British lending rates.
In precious metals, gold prices rose from the level at the morning fix which was near a 12-year low.

The German and Italian bourses were the best performers, hitting intra-day peaks during the day's trading. Paris also climbed strongly but London, Europe's biggest stock exchange, made only modest gains.

Frankfurt continued its cracking pace, with the DAX index surging 1.25 percent to yet another closing record at 4,055.86 points, underpinned by the rising dollar, which boosts prospects for German exporters.
"There seems to be nothing around to brake us at the moment," said a Frankfurt trader.

"The dollar is giving us a push, Bunds(government bonds) are helping, the U.S. is helping and there are no negative corporate stories out there. I don't see any justification for pulling out, even at these highs," the trader said.

In Milan, stocks and bonds soared to record highs as financial markets were seized by a growing conviction that Italy would be a founder member of European economic and monetary union (EMU), planned for launch in 1999.
"Money is pouring in and it looks like we could see a substantial rerating of Italy," said an equities specialist with a foreign finance house in Milan.
The bourse was swept along by a torrent of money from foreign and domestic investors seeking rich pickings as a programme of sell-offs of state assets gathers pace.

The all-share Mibtel index, which tracks all stocks traded on the exchange, hit 13,943 -- its highest level ever -- while the FIB30 September contract, a stock index futures contract based on the top 30 blue chip stocks also rose to record levels.

The Italian government has made swift progress in restoring order to state accounts and bringing down inflation -- key requirements for EMU membership -- just as France and Germany have run into trouble containing their public sector deficits.
The Paris bourse made gains of over one percent, losing some early gains with investors perhaps disappointed by an unsteady start on Wall Street after another record close ion New York on Tuesday.

New York's recent strength has been behind much of the progress on European bourses. Tuesday's close was the 30th record finish this year for the world's most widely watched stock index but the Dow Jones industrials were down slightly at the European mid-afternoon.
London's advance was more modest, with investors distracted by concerns over a two-day Bank of England meeting on interest rates starting on Wednesday but with no decision expected until Thursday.
The blue-chip FTSE index started trade down about 0.5 percent but managed to claw back the early losses to show gains of a few points towards the end of trade.
Many analysts were predicting an increase of at least 25 basis points to curb inflationary pressures.

In currencies, the dollar slipped slightly after climbing to 1.7650 marks, its highest level since February 1994. The Germany currency has been hurt by a subdued economic outlook for the country after Bonn reported a rise of 11,000 in unemployment for June.
"The dollar's just grinding higher, there's no real fresh news to add to the same old story of a solid U.S. economy against a generally weak Europe," said a U.S. bank dealer.

The dollar also climbed slightly on the yen despite a big increase in Japan's May current account surplus. Analysts said the surplus was likely to keep a lid on dollar gains against the yen for the foreseeable future.
Sterling eased back after leaping to a new six-year peak of 2.9760 marks as traders awaited the likely rise in interest rates. It was at 2.9735 marks by mid-afternoon.

"The market continues to have 3.00 marks in its sights and it looks increasingly likely that we will push through this level over a one-month horizon," said Michael Lewis, economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
On bullion markets, gold was fixed in the afternoon at $317.30 after a morning fix of $315.75, its lowest fix since December 11, 1985.

On New York's Commodity Exchange, August gold tumbled in early trading to $316.20 before recovering to $318, a loss of $3 from Tuesday's close. Despite the gloom, producers say physical demand for gold remains strong and they believe that the precious metal will recover.

Gold prices have collapsed since the Reserve Bank of Australia last Thursday said it had sold 167 tonnes of gold from its reserves over the past six months. This triggered heavy selling on fears other banks might follow the example.
CURRENCIES AT 1445 GMT
The dollar was at 112.75 yen and 1.7624 marks compared to 112.57 and 1.7594 in late European trade on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1445 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 6.7 points at 4,765.2.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index ended up 49.46 points at 4,055.86.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 24.91 points at 2,954.72.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in the afternoon at $317.30 per ounce, compared to Tuesday's close of $321.95. Silver was at $4.27, down nine cents.
